Bash
{
  "command": "mkdir -p /Users/durgeshparekh/Documents/GitHub/byte_beam_project && cat > /Users/durgeshparekh/Documents/GitHub/byte_beam_project/ARCHITECTURE.md <<'DOC'\n# Fleet Console \u2014 System Design\n\nFlutter take-home, Bytebeam SDE-3. Local-first fleet telemetry console over embedded DuckDB.\n\nStatus: **design only, nothing built yet.**\n\n---\n\n## 0. The one idea\n\n> **Derived state is a pure fold over an append-only event log. Late or duplicate data is handled by replaying the affected suffix, never by patching.**\n\nEverything hard in this brief \u2014 duplicates, out-of-order packets, GPS jitter, backlog dumps, geofence edits, trip revision \u2014 collapses into that sentence. Alerts, geofence transitions and trips are *never* mutated in place by an incoming packet. They are recomputed from the log for the window the packet touches. Recompute is idempotent because the derivation is a pure function of `(event log \u2229 [t0, \u221e), config)`.\n\nThe corollary is the invariant worth testing above all others:\n\n> Shuffle the packet stream arbitrarily, replay duplicates, and the final derived state must be byte-identical to the in-order replay.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Layout\n\n```\nlib/\n  db/          schema.sql \u00b7 migrations \u00b7 DuckDbService (isolate, connections)\n  ingest/      PacketSource (simulator) \u00b7 IngestPipeline \u00b7 Backfill\n  derive/      SQL derivation: latest \u00b7 alerts \u00b7 transitions \u00b7 trips\n  query/       read-side queries returning plain Dart records\n  features/    fleet \u00b7 vehicle \u00b7 alerts \u00b7 geofences \u00b7 trips  (Riverpod + widgets)\ntool/\n  bench.dart           cold start / p50 / p95 / memory harness\n  export_ai_logs.sh    Claude session jsonl -> ai-logs/*.md\nai-logs/       uncurated AI conversation logs (deliverable 3)\n```\n\nNo repository interfaces, no DAO layer, no abstract `TelemetryService`. One implementation each; a swap is a constructor argument, not an abstraction. Query functions return records/freezed models straight from SQL.\n\n### Isolates\n\nDuckDB is a single-writer, MVCC embedded engine. One process, so multiple connections against one instance are fine \u2014 readers get a snapshot while the writer commits.\n\n- **Writer isolate** \u2014 owns ingest, derivation, backfill. Everything that mutates runs here, serialised, in transactions.\n- **UI isolate** \u2014 read-only connection, queries on demand and on a *debounced* change ping (250 ms). A 3-hour backlog dump must not repaint the fleet list 500 times.\n\n`dart_duckdb` exposes a transferable database handle for exactly this. Ingest batches are bounded (\u2264 5k rows / 200 ms per transaction) so a backlog dump never holds a write lock long enough to stall reads.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Schema\n\nLocation is deliberately **not** a signal. Pairing `lat` and `lon` rows by timestamp is pointless work, and every geofence query wants them side by side.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE vehicle (\n  vehicle_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  reg_no     TEXT NOT NULL,\n  model      TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\n-- append-only event log; the source of truth\nCREATE TABLE signal_reading (\n  vehicle_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  signal     TEXT NOT NULL,        -- soc | speed | battery_temp | odometer | range_km | ignition\n  event_ts   TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,   -- from the packet\n  value      DOUBLE  NOT NULL,     -- booleans as 0/1\n  ingest_ts  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,   -- audit only, never drives logic\n  PRIMARY KEY (vehicle_id, signal, event_ts)\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE location_fix (\n  vehicle_id  TEXT NOT NULL,\n  event_ts    TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,\n  lat DOUBLE NOT NULL, lon DOUBLE NOT NULL,\n  accuracy_m  DOUBLE,\n  ingest_ts   TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,\n  PRIMARY KEY (vehicle_id, event_ts)\n);\n\n-- 500 vehicles x ~6 signals = ~3k rows. The whole read path lives here.\nCREATE TABLE vehicle_signal_latest (\n  vehicle_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  signal     TEXT NOT NULL,\n  event_ts   TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,\n  value      DOUBLE NOT NULL,\n  PRIMARY KEY (vehicle_id, signal)\n);\n\n-- config as data, not as Dart constants: the UI, the verdict pills and the\n-- alert evaluator all read the same row.\nCREATE TABLE signal_spec (\n  signal TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  label TEXT, unit TEXT,\n  max_age_sec INTEGER,      -- older than this => STALE\n  warn_lo DOUBLE, warn_hi DOUBLE,\n  crit_lo DOUBLE, crit_hi DOUBLE\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE geofence (\n  geofence_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  lat DOUBLE, lon DOUBLE, radius_m DOUBLE,\n  active_from TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,     -- activation is time-versioned\n  active_to   TIMESTAMP,              -- NULL = still active; deactivated fences are retained\n  updated_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE alert (\n  alert_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- deterministic: hash(vehicle_id, type, raised_at)\n  vehicle_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  alert_type TEXT NOT NULL,           -- battery_low (escalating) | battery_overheat\n  severity   TEXT NOT NULL,           -- warning | critical\n  raised_at  TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,      -- event time\n  escalated_at TIMESTAMP,\n  resolved_at  TIMESTAMP,\n  dismissed_at TIMESTAMP,\n  dismiss_reason TEXT\n);\n\n-- derived, fully recomputable\nCREATE TABLE geofence_transition (\n  vehicle_id TEXT, geofence_id TEXT,\n  event_ts TIMESTAMP,                 -- time of the crossing fix, not the confirming fix\n  kind TEXT,                          -- ENTRY | EXIT\n  confidence TEXT,                    -- high | low (crossed a data gap)\n  PRIMARY KEY (vehicle_id, geofence_id, event_ts)\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE trip (\n  trip_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- deterministic: hash(vehicle_id, start_ts)\n  vehicle_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n  origin_geofence_id TEXT, start_ts TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,\n  dest_geofence_id   TEXT, end_ts   TIMESTAMP,\n  status TEXT NOT NULL,               -- IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED\n  distance_km DOUBLE,                 -- odometer delta, NULL if unavailable\n  confidence TEXT\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE ingest_watermark (\n  vehicle_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n  processed_through TIMESTAMP NOT NULL\n);\n```\n\n`signal_reading` is the only large table. Its 3-column ART primary key is what makes duplicate rejection O(log n) instead of a table scan \u2014 and it is the first thing I will look at if memory at rest disappoints (see \u00a77).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Ingest\n\nOne transaction per batch, in the writer isolate:\n\n1. **Dedupe within the batch** \u2014 keep `max(event_ts)` per `(vehicle_id, signal)`.\n2. **Append** \u2014 `INSERT \u2026 ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Idempotency is now a database constraint, not a code path.\n3. **Advance latest** \u2014 the only tricky upsert. A late packet must never clobber a newer reading:\n\n```sql\nINSERT INTO vehicle_signal_latest AS l (vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value)\nSELECT vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value FROM batch\nON CONFLICT (vehicle_id, signal) DO UPDATE\n  SET value = excluded.value, event_ts = excluded.event_ts\n  WHERE excluded.event_ts > l.event_ts;\n```\n\n4. **Detect regression** \u2014 if `min(event_ts)` in the batch for a vehicle is older than its `ingest_watermark`, that vehicle needs a replay from `min(event_ts) \u2212 lookback`. Otherwise, incremental derivation from the watermark forward.\n5. **Derive** \u2014 alerts, transitions, trips (\u00a75, \u00a76).\n6. **Advance watermark**, commit, ping the UI.\n\nDerivation runs **in SQL**, not Dart. Pulling the log into Dart to fold over it is precisely the in-memory-shadow the brief rules out, and it makes recompute over a large window unaffordable. The rules (hysteresis, debounce, thresholds) live in config tables so tests can vary them without touching SQL.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Fleet list\n\nThe whole read path is ~3k rows, so the query is trivially fast and no caching is warranted.\n\n```sql\nWITH p AS (\n  SELECT vehicle_id,\n         max(event_ts)                                   AS last_ping,\n         max(value)    FILTER (signal = 'soc')           AS soc,\n         max(event_ts) FILTER (signal = 'soc')           AS soc_ts,\n         max(value)    FILTER (signal = 'speed')         AS speed,\n         max(event_ts) FILTER (signal = 'speed')         AS speed_ts,\n         max(value)    FILTER (signal = 'ignition')      AS ignition,\n         max(event_ts) FILTER (signal = 'ignition')      AS ignition_ts,\n         max(value)    FILTER (signal = 'range_km')      AS range_km\n  FROM vehicle_signal_latest GROUP BY vehicle_id\n)\nSELECT v.reg_no, v.model, p.soc, p.range_km,\n  CASE\n    WHEN p.last_ping IS NULL OR p.last_ping < $now - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE THEN 'OFFLINE'\n    WHEN p.speed    > 0 AND p.speed_ts    >= $now - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE   THEN 'MOVING'\n    WHEN p.speed    = 0 AND p.speed_ts    >= $now - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE\n     AND p.ignition = 1 AND p.ignition_ts >= $now - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE   THEN 'IDLE'\n    ELSE 'STOPPED'\n  END AS status\nFROM vehicle v LEFT JOIN p USING (vehicle_id);\n```\n\n`last_ping` is `max(event_ts)` over all signals **and** location fixes for that vehicle. Filter chip counts are `GROUP BY status` over the same CTE \u2014 one query, computed in SQL, never in Dart.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Alerts\n\nEvaluated over `vehicle_signal_latest \u22c8 signal_spec`, **fresh readings only**, after every ingest batch.\n\n| Alert | Condition | Severity |\n|---|---|---|\n| `battery_low` | SOC < 20 % | warning |\n| `battery_low` | SOC < 10 % | **critical** (same row, escalated) |\n| `battery_overheat` | battery_temp > 45 \u00b0C | critical |\n\nThe two SOC alerts are one row whose `severity` moves warning \u21c4 critical. Recovering from 8 % to 15 % de-escalates in place; it does not resolve and re-raise.\n\n**Dismissal.** Sheet order is fixed: *I am on it* \u00b7 *Wrong alert* \u00b7 *Something else\u2026*. The dismissal is written to DuckDB immediately and UNDO clears `dismissed_at`. It is not held in memory for 5 seconds \u2014 local-first means the database is the truth, and if the app dies mid-window the dismissal stands. That is the honest trade; the alternative loses a user's explicit action to a crash.\n\n**Resolution is independent.** The evaluator clears an alert when its condition clears, dismissed or not. A dismissed alert whose condition never clears simply stays hidden until the condition clears and re-triggers \u2014 dismissal suppresses the *episode*, not the *rule*.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Geofences and trips\n\n### 6.1 Transition detection\n\nDeterministic pipeline, applied per `(vehicle, geofence)` over event-time-ordered fixes:\n\n1. **Accuracy gate** \u2014 discard fixes with `accuracy_m > 100`. Filtered at read; nothing is ever deleted from the log.\n2. **Hysteresis** \u2014 inside if `d \u2264 r \u2212 h`, outside if `d \u2265 r + h`, with `h = max(25 m, accuracy_m)`. Fixes in the band produce **no zone opinion**.\n3. **Carry forward** \u2014 `last_value(zone IGNORE NULLS) OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id, geofence_id ORDER BY event_ts)`. The band is now genuinely inert rather than a source of flapping.\n4. **Confirm** \u2014 a crossing is confirmed when two consecutive opinionated fixes agree on the new zone. Escape hatch for a fast exit: one fix more than `2h` past the boundary confirms alone.\n5. **Timestamp** \u2014 the transition is stamped with the **first** fix of the confirming pair. That is when the vehicle actually crossed.\n6. **Gaps** \u2014 if the confirming pair straddles a gap > 30 min (the basement case), the transition is still recorded but flagged `confidence = 'low'`, and any trip built on it inherits that flag. Nothing is synthesised across a gap.\n7. **Overlaps** \u2014 no single \"current geofence\" internally; containment is per fence. The UI's single-value *current geofence* is the **smallest radius containing the vehicle**, tie-broken by `geofence_id`.\n8. **Fence activation** is time-versioned via `active_from` / `active_to`, so evaluation asks \"was this fence active at the fix's event time\" and recompute stays pure. **Geometry is not versioned** \u2014 editing centre or radius triggers a full recompute of that fence's transitions and the affected trips. Full geometry versioning is the upgrade if fences turn out to be edited often; it is not worth the table for this exercise.\n\nAll of steps 2\u20136 are expressible with `lag`/`last_value IGNORE NULLS` window functions \u2014 set-based, no row-at-a-time Dart fold.\n\n### 6.2 Trips\n\nA nested fence must not manufacture a trip: leaving a bay while still inside the depot is not a departure. So trips key off **containment count**, not individual fences:\n\n```sql\nSELECT *, sum(CASE kind WHEN 'ENTRY' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END)\n            OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id ORDER BY event_ts) AS inside_count\nFROM geofence_transition\n```\n\n- `inside_count` falling to **0** \u2192 trip starts; origin = the fence just exited.\n- `inside_count` rising off 0 \u2192 active trip completes; destination = the fence just entered. Returning to origin is a normal completion.\n- Still 0 at the end of the stream \u2192 `IN_PROGRESS`. No timeout; a truck that never reports again keeps an open trip, which is the truthful representation.\n- One active trip per vehicle falls out of the model for free.\n- Incremental recompute seeds `inside_count` from the containment state at the window start.\n\n`distance_km` comes from an `ASOF JOIN` onto the odometer log at `start_ts` and `end_ts`; NULL when the odometer is missing rather than guessed.\n\n**Idempotency.** `trip_id = hash(vehicle_id, start_ts)`, so a duplicate packet regenerates the identical row. A late packet that moves a boundary is handled by the replay in \u00a73 step 4 \u2014 delete derived rows at or after `t0`, re-derive \u2014 with the deterministic id as the backstop, not the mechanism.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Scale\n\n**Backfill.** 500 vehicles \u00d7 6 signals \u00d7 ~700 ticks \u2248 2.1 M rows, generated **inside DuckDB** with `range()` and `random()` in a single `INSERT \u2026 SELECT`. Generating rows in Dart and pushing them across the FFI boundary would take minutes; this takes seconds. The table is created without the primary key, bulk-loaded, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` once \u2014 building the ART index in one pass instead of 2 M times.\n\n**Measurements to report**, on a named physical device plus a named emulator:\n\n| Metric | How | Target |\n|---|---|---|\n| Cold start \u2192 first painted fleet list | stopwatch from `main()`, stopped in `addTimingsCallback` on first frame with data | < 2.5 s |\n| Fleet-list query p50 / p95, warm | 100 runs in the writer isolate, dumped to CSV | p95 < 25 ms |\n| Memory at rest, list open | `adb shell dumpsys meminfo` PSS, DevTools cross-check | < 250 MB |\n\nIf a number is bad it gets reported as bad, with a diagnosis. The two I already expect to be the suspects:\n\n- **Cold start** is dominated by opening the database and loading the ART index, not by the query. Mitigation: open and run the fleet query in the writer isolate before the first frame and paint a skeleton.\n- **Memory at rest** is dominated by that same index on a 2 M-row table. If it dominates, the fix is to drop the primary key and dedupe with an ANTI JOIN against a bounded recent window \u2014 duplicates only ever arrive near the present, so a full-history index earns nothing.\n\n**Retention.** An append-only log grows forever, so:\n\n- `signal_reading` keeps 7 days at full resolution.\n- Older data is downsampled into 5-minute buckets per `(vehicle, signal)` \u2014 min/max/avg/last \u2014 and the raw rows are dropped, followed by `CHECKPOINT`.\n- Derived tables (transitions, trips, alerts) are small and kept indefinitely.\n- **What is lost:** sub-5-minute shape of old data, and the ability to *recompute* geofence transitions outside the hot window. Trip replay is therefore bounded to 7 days; a late packet older than that is rejected and counted, not silently applied.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Tests\n\nThe suite is built around the invariant from \u00a70, not around line coverage.\n\n**The test that matters:** generate a packet stream, shuffle it, inject duplicates and delays, replay it, and assert the derived state \u2014 latest values, alerts, transitions, trips \u2014 is identical to the in-order replay. If that holds, the concurrency and late-data story holds.\n\nAround it, fixture-driven SQL tests against an in-memory DuckDB (fast, no Flutter binding):\n\n- duplicate packet \u00b7 out-of-order packet \u00b7 backlog dump\n- GPS jitter parked on the boundary \u2192 **zero** transitions\n- fast exit confirmed by a single distant fix\n- data gap \u2192 transition present, `confidence = 'low'`\n- nested fences \u2192 exiting the inner bay starts no trip\n- return-to-origin trip completes\n- fence geometry edit \u2192 transitions and trips recomputed\n- fence deactivated \u2192 prior transitions retained, no new ones\n- SOC 18 \u2192 8 escalates in place (one alert row, not two)\n- dismiss then escalate \u2192 alert reappears\n- condition clears while dismissed \u2192 resolved\n- signal goes stale while alerting \u2192 **not** resolved\n- never-reported signal \u2192 \"\u2014\", no pill\n\nPlus widget tests for the fleet list statuses and chip counts, the dismissal sheet ordering and the 5-second undo, and one integration test that backfills 10 vehicles and asserts row counts and query sanity.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Ambiguities and how they are resolved\n\nThe brief says the data model has genuinely ambiguous cases. These are the ones I found and the calls I made.\n\n| # | Ambiguity | Resolution | Rejected alternative |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Vehicle is online (odometer 2 min old) but `speed` is 40 min old. MOVING? | Status only reads **fresh** signals; a stale speed cannot claim MOVING or IDLE, so it falls through to STOPPED. STOPPED is the documented fallback bucket. | A sixth `UNKNOWN` chip \u2014 the brief specifies five. |\n| 2 | What is \"last ping\"? | `max(event_ts)` across all signals *and* location fixes for the vehicle. | Per-signal freshness only \u2014 the brief says vehicle-level. |\n| 3 | Event time or arrival time? | **Event time** drives every rule: freshness, status, alerts, transitions, trips. `ingest_ts` is audit only. | Arrival time \u2014 makes a backlog dump look like a fleet that just woke up. |\n| 4 | What is a duplicate? | Identity is `(vehicle_id, signal, event_ts)`. Same key, different value \u2192 keep the first, increment a conflict counter surfaced in a debug view. | Last-write-wins \u2014 non-deterministic under reordering, which breaks \u00a70. |\n| 5 | Packet older than the retention window | Rejected and counted. It cannot be replayed correctly, so applying it would produce state that no longer follows from the log. | Silently inserting it and leaving derived state inconsistent. |\n| 6 | Signal goes stale while an alert is open | Alert stays open, shown with a stale marker. | Auto-resolve \u2014 that hides a truck that died at 5 % SOC. |\n| 7 | Dismissed at 18 %, then SOC hits 8 % | Escalation clears `dismissed_at` and re-raises. \"I am on it\" at 18 % is not consent to ignore 8 %. | Staying dismissed through escalation. |\n| 8 | UNDO window vs. app kill | Dismissal is persisted immediately; UNDO clears it. Killed mid-window \u2192 dismissal stands. | Holding it in memory for 5 s \u2014 loses an explicit user action to a crash. |\n| 9 | Geofence edited after history exists | Activation is time-versioned; **geometry is not** \u2014 a geometry edit recomputes that fence's transitions and affected trips. | Full geometry versioning (correct, more table than this earns) or forward-only edits (cheap, but derived state stops being reproducible from the log). |\n| 10 | Vehicle inside two overlapping fences | Containment tracked per fence. UI \"current geofence\" = smallest radius containing it, tie-break `geofence_id`. | A single current-fence column \u2014 undefined under nesting. |\n| 11 | Exiting a bay inside a depot | Trips key off containment count reaching 0, so leaving the inner fence starts nothing. | Per-fence exit starts a trip \u2014 one departure would produce two trips. |\n| 12 | Trip whose vehicle never reports again | Stays `IN_PROGRESS` forever. | A 24-hour abandonment timeout \u2014 invents an ending the data does not support. |\n| 13 | GPS jitter on the boundary | 25 m (or accuracy, whichever larger) hysteresis band plus two-fix confirmation; band fixes carry the previous zone forward. | Bare `d < r` \u2014 flaps a parked truck into dozens of trips. |\n\n---\n\n## 10. Scope cuts\n\nStated up front, per the brief.\n\n- **No backend, no auth, no sync.** The packet source is a simulator behind a one-method interface; a real MQTT/HTTP feed is a constructor swap.\n- **No map tiles in v1.** Geofences are created and edited by name / lat / lon / radius with a schematic canvas preview. `flutter_map` goes in only if time remains after tests \u2014 it is presentation, and every ambiguity above is decided without it.\n- **No background ingest while the app is killed.** No foreground service, no WorkManager.\n- **No severity/escalation audit trail.** The alert row carries `escalated_at`; the full state-change log is a table I would add the moment anyone asked \"why did this fire\".\n- **No i18n, no custom theme.** Material 3 defaults.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Deliverables plan\n\n**Commits** \u2014 phased, in my own words, no squash: schema \u2192 ingest + dedupe \u2192 fleet list \u2192 vehicle detail + verdicts \u2192 alerts \u2192 geofences \u2192 transitions \u2192 trips \u2192 backfill + bench \u2192 tests \u2192 README.\n\n**README** \u2014 run the app, run the tests, 30-second feature tour, plus the measured numbers from \u00a77 and the device they came from.\n\n**AI logs** \u2014 `ai-logs/`, uncurated, committed as work proceeds so the dead ends stay in the history rather than being tidied away at the end. `tool/export_ai_logs.sh` converts the raw Claude Code session transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl`) into chronological markdown. Two practical notes: run Claude from the project root so its sessions land in one slug directory, and export after every session \u2014 the transcripts are the deliverable, and a curated summary is explicitly not what was asked for.\nDOC\nwc -l /Users/durgeshparekh/Documents/GitHub/byte_beam_project/ARCHITECTURE.md",

### Claude — 2026-09-12T06:55:37.232Z
Read the PDF (had to un-ASCII85 it — no poppler on this box). Design written.

**[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** — 11 sections. The spine:

**One idea:** derived state is a pure fold over the append-only log. Late/duplicate/reordered packets are handled by replaying the affected suffix, never by patching. Alerts, transitions and trips all fall out of that, and it gives you the one test worth writing: *shuffle the stream, inject duplicates, assert the final state equals in-order replay.*

**Concrete calls:**
- `signal_reading` PK `(vehicle, signal, event_ts)` → dedupe is a DB constraint, not a code path. Location gets its own table, not two paired signals.
- `vehicle_signal_latest` (~3k rows) is the entire read path — fleet list + chip counts are one SQL query over it, with a conditional `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE excluded.event_ts > l.event_ts` so late packets can't clobber.
- Derivation in SQL window functions (`last_value … IGNORE NULLS`, `lag`, ASOF join), not a Dart fold — a Dart fold *is* the in-memory shadow the brief forbids.
- Jitter: 25 m hysteresis band + two-fix confirmation; band fixes carry the previous zone forward. Trips key off **containment count hitting 0**, not per-fence exits — so leaving a bay inside a depot starts nothing, and "one active trip" is free.
- Backfill generates 2.1 M rows *inside* DuckDB via `range()`, index built after load.

**§9 is the section they're actually grading** — 13 ambiguities in a table with the call and the rejected alternative (stale speed → STOPPED; stale signal does *not* resolve an alert; escalation un-dismisses; geometry not versioned but activation is; late packet past retention rejected and counted).

Also added **[tool/export_ai_logs.sh](tool/export_ai_logs.sh)** — dumps Claude session jsonl → `ai-logs/*.md`, uncurated, tool calls included. Smoke-tested against a real transcript dir (34 turns out clean). Run it from the project root or the slug won't match.

skipped: map tiles, backend, escalation audit trail — all listed in §10 with when to add. Two `dart_duckdb` assumptions to verify in the first spike: transferable DB across isolates, and `ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE … WHERE`.

Waiting for your instruction. Want this as a shareable page too, or is the repo file enough?

## 4. Ingest

One transaction per batch, in the writer isolate:

1. **Dedupe within the batch** — keep `max(event_ts)` per `(vehicle_id, signal)`.
2. **Append** — `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Idempotency is now a database constraint, not a code path.
3. **Advance latest** — the only tricky upsert. A late packet must never clobber a newer reading:

```sql
INSERT INTO vehicle_signal_latest AS l (vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value)
SELECT vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value FROM batch
ON CONFLICT (vehicle_id, signal) DO UPDATE
  SET value = excluded.value, event_ts = excluded.event_ts
  WHERE excluded.event_ts > l.event_ts;
```

4. **Detect regression** — if `min(event_ts)` in the batch for a vehicle is older than its `ingest_watermark`, that vehicle needs a replay from `min(event_ts) − lookback`. Otherwise, incremental derivation from the watermark forward.
5. **Derive** — alerts, transitions, trips (§6, §7).
6. **Advance watermark**, commit, ping the UI.

Derivation runs **in SQL**, not Dart. Pulling the log into Dart to fold over it is precisely the in-memory-shadow the brief rules out, and it makes recompute over a large window unaffordable. The rules (hysteresis, debounce, thresholds) live in config tables so tests can vary them without touching SQL.

---

## 5. Fleet list
```

### Claude — 2026-09-12T07:47:21.703Z
Added as **§3 in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** (renumbered the rest; §4 ingest now matches).

The whole answer is one classification: **who owns the truth for each row.** That decides sync direction, conflict rule, transaction boundary, and whether the table is disposable.

| Class | Tables | Sync | Conflict | On loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R** remote-authoritative, immutable | `vehicle`, `signal_reading`, `location_fix` | pull, cursored | impossible by construction | re-pullable |
| **L** device-authored intent | `geofence`, alert dismissal | push, via outbox | per-table rule | **the only losable data** |
| **D** derived | `vehicle_signal_latest`, transitions, trips | never | n/a | dropped and rebuilt |

Four things that fall out of it:

**Natural key + cursor-in-the-same-transaction means at-least-once delivery is enough.** No exactly-once protocol. Crash between fetch and commit → re-pull, the constraint absorbs it. Dedupe is the *side effect* of the natural key, not its purpose.

**Class R is never row-updated.** DuckDB is OLAP — a per-row `UPDATE` on a 2 M-row table is a rewrite. Confining all mutation to the few-thousand-row tables isn't tidiness, it's the reason the schema is shaped this way.

**Outbox: entity row and outbox row in one transaction.** "Saved locally but never queued" stops being a representable state. `op_id` = UUIDv7 = idempotency key *and* replay order. Pending ops coalesce per entity so a week in a basement doesn't queue a week of work. Conflict rules are per-table, deliberately: geofence is LWW on `updated_at`, but **alert dismissal is earliest-wins** — a dismissal is a monotonic acknowledgement, and LWW would let a late-reconnecting device overwrite the fact that a colleague was already on it. A blanket LWW policy is the smell.

**Two transactions per ingest batch, watermark last.** Derived state is always behind the log, never ahead — so there is no recovery routine. A crash mid-batch leaves a state identical to normal operation, repaired by the same "derive from watermark" call every batch makes. Crash recovery gets exercised by every test instead of by a special one nobody runs.

Class D also drops out of the migration surface entirely (drop + rebuild), leaving only the small Class L tables needing real migrations.

skipped: the outbox is designed, not built — no backend in this scope (§11), so it'd be a queue with no consumer. The cursor is real, because the simulator is a positioned replayable source. Add the outbox the commit after a server exists.

abstract class DuckDB {

  Future<Connection> connect(
    Database database, {
    String? id,
  });

  Future<Connection> connectWithTransferred(
    TransferableDatabase transferableDb, {
    String? id,

=== database ===
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dart_duckdb/src/types/protocol.dart';

/// An opened duckdb database with `dart:ffi`.
abstract class Database {
  /// The native database connection handle from duckdb.
  ///
  /// This returns a pointer towards the opaque duckdb structure as defined
  dynamic get handle;

  /// An unmanaged database reference that can be sent across isolate boundaries.
  /// Disposing the source database, will invalidate this TransferableDatabase.
  ///
  /// Use this to create [Connection]s on separate isolates.
  /// It is recommended to have a single connection per isolate.
  TransferableDatabase get transferable;

  /// Register a file buffer with the database.
  /// This is only for duckdb-wasm.
  Future<void> registerFileBuffer(String name, Uint8List buffer);

  /// Register a file URL with the database.
  /// This is only for duckdb-wasm.
  Future<void> registerFileURL(
    String name,
    String url,
    DuckDBDataProtocol protocol,
    bool directIO,
  );

  /// Register a file handle with the database.
  /// This is only for duckdb-wasm.
  Future<void> registerFileHandle(
    String name,
    dynamic handle,
    DuckDBDataProtocol protocol,
    bool directIO,
  );

  /// Closes this database and releases associated resources.
  Future<void> dispose();
}

/// A database weak reference that can be sent across isolate boundaries.
abstract class TransferableDatabase {}

/// A DuckDB connection implemented
abstract class Connection {
  /// The native DuckDB connection handle pointer
  dynamic get handle;

  /// The id of the connection
  String? get id;

  /// Executes a query and returns the result set
  /// Can be cancelled via token
  Future<ResultSet> query(String query, {DuckDBCancellationToken? token});

  /// Executes a query without returning results
  /// Can be cancelled,but not interrupted via token
  Future<void> execute(String query, {DuckDBCancellationToken? token});

  /// Creates a prepared statement from a query
  /// Can be cancelled,but not interrupted via token
  Future<PreparedStatement> prepare(
    String query, {
    DuckDBCancellationToken? token,
  });

  /// Creates an appender for inserting data into a table
  Future<Appender> append(String table, String? schema);

  /// Gets the ordered column names for a table
  Future<Iterable<String>> getColumnOrder(String table);

  /// Interrupts the currently running operation
  Future<void> interrupt();

  /// Closes the connection and frees resources
  Future<void> dispose();
}

import 'package:dart_duckdb/src/api/column.dart';
import 'package:dart_duckdb/src/api/database_type.dart';

/// An object representing a DuckDB result set
///
/// A DuckDB result set contains the data returned from the database after a
/// successful query.
///
/// A result set is organized into vertical table slices called columns.
abstract class ResultSet {
  /// The number of columns in the result set
  int get columnCount;

  /// The total number of rows in the result set
  int get rowCount;

  /// The names of the columns in the result set
  List<String> get columnNames;

  static DuckDB? instance;

      : _library = BindingsWithLibrary(
          (load.open as load.OpenDynamicLibrary).openDuckDB(),
        );

  Future<Connection> connect(Database database, {String? id}) async {
    return ConnectionImpl.connect(database, id: id);

  @override
  Future<Connection> connectWithTransferred(
    TransferableDatabase transferableDatabase, {
    String? id,
  }) async {

    );

  @override
  String get version {
    return bindings.duckdb_library_version().readString();
  }
}

///
/// The default behavior can be overridden for a specific OS by using
/// [overrideFor]. To override the behavior on all platforms, use
/// [overrideForAll].
class OpenDynamicLibrary extends OpenLibrary {
  final Map<OperatingSystem, OpenLibraryLoader> _overriddenPlatforms = {};

  OpenDynamicLibrary._();

  /// Returns the current [OperatingSystem] as read from the [Platform] getters.
  OperatingSystem? get os {
    if (Platform.isAndroid) return OperatingSystem.android;
    if (Platform.isIOS) return OperatingSystem.iOS;
    if (Platform.isLinux) return OperatingSystem.linux;
    if (Platform.isMacOS) return OperatingSystem.macOS;
    if (Platform.isWindows) return OperatingSystem.windows;
    return null;
  }

  /// Opens the [DynamicLibrary] from which `duckdb.dart` is going to
  /// [DynamicLibrary.lookup] duckdb's methods that will be used. This method is
  /// meant to be called by `duckdb.dart` only.
  DynamicLibrary openDuckDB() {
    /// If the process already provides has the symbol, we can use it directly.
    /// This is useful when we have loaded the library and are now on an isolate.
    final process = DynamicLibrary.process();
    if (process.providesSymbol('duckdb_open')) {
      return process;
    }

    /// If we are in a test environment, we will load the library from the package.
    if (_isTestEnvironment()) {
      final prefix = '${Directory.current.path}/../duckdb';

      if (_overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.windows] == null) {
        _overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.windows] =
            () => DynamicLibrary.open(
                  '$prefix/windows/Libraries/release/duckdb.dll',
                );
      }

      if (_overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.macOS] == null) {
        _overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.macOS] = () => DynamicLibrary.open(
              '$prefix/macos/Libraries/release/libduckdb.dylib',
            );
      }

      if (_overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.linux] == null) {
        _overriddenPlatforms[OperatingSystem.linux] = () => DynamicLibrary.open(
              '$prefix/linux/Libraries/release/libduckdb.so',
            );
      }
    }

    try {
      final forPlatform = _overriddenPlatforms[os];
      if (forPlatform != null) {
        return forPlatform();
      }
    } catch (error) {
      // ignore
    }

    return _defaultOpen();
  }

  /// Makes `duckdb.dart` use the [open] function when running on the specified
  /// [os]. This can be used to override the loading behavior on some platforms.
  /// To override that behavior on all platforms, consider using
  /// [overrideForAll].
  /// This method must be called before opening any database.
  ///
  /// When using the asynchronous API over isolates, [open] __must be__ a top-
  /// level function or a static method.
  @override
  void overrideFor(OperatingSystem os, String path) {
    _overriddenPlatforms[os] = () => DynamicLibrary.open(path);
  }

  /// Clears all associated open helpers for all platforms.
  @visibleForTesting
  @override
  void reset() {
    _overriddenPlatforms.clear();
  }
}

/// The instance managing different approaches to load the [DynamicLibrary] for
/// duckdb when needed. See the documentation for [OpenDynamicLibrary] to learn
/// how the default opening behavior can be overridden.
final OpenLibrary open = OpenDynamicLibrary._();

One instance per process \u2014 DuckDB takes a file lock,\n/// so extra isolates attach through [transferable] rather than reopening.\n///\n/// This library is deliberately Flutter-free so the DB tests run on the plain\n/// Dart VM. The app supplies the file path (see `lib/main.dart`).\nclass FleetDb {\n  FleetDb._(this._db, this.read);\n\n  final Database _db;\n\n  /// Read-only-by-convention connection for the UI isolate. DuckDB is MVCC,\n  /// so this sees a consistent snapshot while the writer commits.\n  final Connection read;\n\n  /// Pass to [inIsolate] to get a connection on another isolate.\n  TransferableDatabase get transferable => _db.transferable;\n\n  /// Opens [path] (`:memory:` for a throwaway db) and migrates it forward.\n  static Future<FleetDb> open(String path) async {\n    final db = await duckdb.open(path);\n    final conn = await duckdb.connect(db);\n    await _migrate(conn);\n    return FleetDb._(db, conn);\n  }\n\n  /// Runs [job] on its own isolate with its own connection.\n  ///\n  /// [job] must be a top-level or static function: it is sent across an\n  /// isolate boundary, so anything it closes over has to be sendable too.\n  static Future<R> inIsolate<R>(\n    TransferableDatabase transferable,\n    Future<R> Function(Connection) job,\n  ) {\n    return Isolate.run(() async {\n      final conn = await duckdb.connectWithTransferred(transferable);\n      try {\n        return await job(conn);\n      } finally {\n        await conn.dispose();\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  Future<void> close() async {\n    await read.dispose();\n    await _db.dispose();\n  }\n}\n\n/// Forward-only migrations, applied in one transaction each so a crash\n/// mid-upgrade leaves the previous version intact rather than a half-schema.\nFuture<void> _migrate(Connection conn) async {\n  await conn.execute(\n    'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)',\n  );\n  final result = await conn.query(\n    'SELECT coalesce(max(version), 0) FROM schema_version',\n  );\n  final applied = (result.fetchOne()!.first as num).toInt();\n\n  for (var version = applied + 1; `lib/db/` is Flutter-free, so DB tests run on the plain VM. Schema is a Dart string, not a bundled `.sql` — the writer isolate has no `rootBundle`, and migrations run there.

**Verified, not assumed:**
- 9/9 tests pass; `flutter build macos` and `flutter build apk` both green, `libduckdb.so` in the APK for arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a; the macOS app creates and reopens `fleet.duckdb` in Application Support.
- `test/db/fleet_db_test.dart` pins the three things §1 rests on: a writer on a spawned isolate, a reader on the main one seeing its commit, and the data still there after close-and-reopen.
- `test/db/duckdb_features_test.dart` pins every SQL feature ARCHITECTURE.md leans on — conditional `ON CONFLICT … WHERE excluded.event_ts > l.event_ts`, `last_value(… IGNORE NULLS)`, `FILTER`, `ASOF JOIN`, `range()`, PK dedupe. A DuckDB bump that breaks one now fails here instead of in the app. It already earned its keep: my doc had `FILTER (signal = …)`, the real syntax is `FILTER (WHERE …)` — doc corrected.

**Two things worth knowing:**

`dart_duckdb` is pinned to **1.2.2 exactly**, not `^1.2.0`. Packages 1.4.1–1.4.4 point their Android Gradle task at release tags with no Android binaries — `v1.4.1` and `v1.4.4` both 404, so the APK cannot build. 1.2.2 pulls from `v1.2.0`, which exists. That's almost certainly why the brief names `^1.2.0`. Engine is DuckDB 1.2.1, and `tool/fetch_duckdb_lib.sh` fetches that same version so host tests and device run identical SQL.

`flutter test` needs `tool/fetch_duckdb_lib.sh` run once — the package's own test-mode fallback points at paths inside its monorepo, which don't exist in a consumer app. One line in the README.

They keep their original event time.\n  final List<_DelayedPacket> _delayed = [];\n\n  StreamController<List<TelemetryPacket>>? _controller;\n  Timer? _timer;\n  int _tickCount = 0;\n\n  @override\n  List<FleetVehicle> get fleet => [\n        for (final vehicle in _vehicles)\n          FleetVehicle(\n            vehicleId: vehicle.id,\n            regNo: vehicle.regNo,\n            model: vehicle.model,\n          ),\n      ];\n\n  /// Starts the timer and emits a batch per configured tick.\n  ///\n  /// Single-subscription: the repository is the only listener, and the\n  /// controller pauses the timer when nobody is listening.\n  @override\n  Stream<List<TelemetryPacket>> stream() {\n    final controller = _controller ??= StreamController<List<TelemetryPacket>>(\n      onCancel: dispose,\n    );\n    _timer ??= Timer.periodic(config.tick, (_) {\n      if (controller.isClosed) return;\n      final batch = generateTick();\n      if (batch.isNotEmpty) controller.add(batch);\n    });\n    return controller.stream;\n  }\n\n  @override\n  Future<void> dispose() async {\n    _timer?.cancel();\n    _timer = null;\n    await _controller?.close();\n    _controller = null;\n  }\n\n  /// Produces exactly one tick's worth of arrivals.\n  ///\n  /// Public and synchronous so tests can drive the simulator without real\n  /// timers \u2014 the fault injection is the part worth asserting on, and waiting\n  /// half a second per tick to observe it would be silly.\n  List<TelemetryPacket> generateTick() {\n    _tickCount++;\n    final now = _clock.nowUtc();\n    final arrivals = <TelemetryPacket>[];\n\n    for (final vehicle in _vehicles) {\n      _advance(vehicle);\n      final packet = _emit(vehicle, now);\n      if (packet.isEmpty) continue;\n      _route(vehicle, packet, arrivals);\n    }\n\n    _releaseDue(arrivals);\n\n    // Arrival order is not emission order on a real link. Shuffling with the\n    // seeded generator keeps that true and still reproducible.\n    arrivals.shuffle(_random);\n    return arrivals;\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------- routing --\n\n  /// Decides what the network does to one freshly measured packet: drop it,\n  /// buffer it behind a dead link, deliver it now, deliver it late, and/or\n  /// deliver it twice.\n  void _route(\n    _SimulatedVehicle vehicle,\n    TelemetryPacket packet,\n    List<TelemetryPacket> arrivals,\n  ) {\n    // A vehicle parked in a basement keeps measuring and keeps nothing\n    // flowing. The backlog lands in one burst when the link returns.\n    if (vehicle.darkTicks > 0) {\n      vehicle.buffer.add(packet);\n      vehicle.darkTicks--;\n      if (vehicle.darkTicks == 0) {\n        arrivals.addAll(vehicle.buffer);\n        vehicle.buffer.clear();\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < config.backlogChance) {\n      vehicle.darkTicks = config.backlogTicks;\n      vehicle.buffer.add(packet);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < config.dropRate) return;\n\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < config.lateRate) {\n      // Held back, but still stamped with when it was measured \u2014 this is the\n      // out-of-order case, not a fresh reading.\n      _delayed.add(_DelayedPacket(packet, _tickCount + 1 + _random.nextInt(4)));\n    } else {\n      arrivals.add(packet);\n    }\n\n    // A retransmit: byte-identical, same event time, so the natural key is\n    // what has to reject it. Sent a tick or two later to exercise the\n    // cross-batch case rather than the easy within-batch one.\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < config.duplicateRate) {\n      _delayed.add(_DelayedPacket(packet, _tickCount + 1 + _random.nextInt(3)));\n    }\n  }\n\n  /// Moves delayed packets into this tick's arrivals once their time is up.\n  void _releaseDue(List<TelemetryPacket> arrivals) {\n    _delayed.removeWhere((delayed) {\n      if (delayed.releaseTick > _tickCount) return false;\n      arrivals.add(delayed.packet);\n      return true;\n    });\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------- physics --\n\n  /// Advances one vehicle by one tick.\n  ///\n  /// Crude on purpose: the pipeline does not care whether the curves are\n  /// right, only that values move plausibly, stay in range, and occasionally\n  /// cross a threshold.\n  void _advance(_SimulatedVehicle vehicle) {\n    final hours = config.tick.inMilliseconds / 3600000.0;\n\n    // Ignition flips rarely, so vehicles hold a state long enough to be worth\n    // looking at in the fleet list.\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < 0.02) vehicle.ignition = !vehicle.ignition;\n\n    if (!vehicle.ignition) {\n      vehicle.speed = 0;\n      vehicle.batteryTemp = _towards(vehicle.batteryTemp, 28, 0.4);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Speed wanders and is occasionally zero \u2014 that is the IDLE case, ignition\n    // on and not moving.\n    vehicle.speed = _random.nextDouble() < 0.25\n        ? 0\n        : (vehicle.speed + (_random.nextDouble() - 0.45) * 18).clamp(0, 80);\n\n    final km = vehicle.speed * hours;\n    vehicle.odometer += km;\n    vehicle.soc = (vehicle.soc - km * vehicle.drainPerKm).clamp(0, 100);\n\n    // Charging: a flat truck plugs in rather than sitting at 0% forever.\n    if (vehicle.soc <= 1) vehicle.soc = 100;\n\n    vehicle.batteryTemp = _towards(\n      vehicle.batteryTemp,\n      28 + vehicle.speed * 0.22 + vehicle.tempBias,\n      0.35,\n    );\n\n    // Straight-line drift with an occasional turn. Good enough to cross a\n    // geofence boundary, which is all the later features need.\n    if (_random.nextDouble() < 0.15) {\n      vehicle.heading = (vehicle.heading + (_random.nextDouble() - 0.5) * 2) % (2 * pi);\n    }\n    vehicle.lat += km / 111.0 * cos(vehicle.heading);\n    vehicle.lon += km / (111.0 * cos(vehicle.lat * pi / 180)) * sin(vehicle.heading);\n  }\n\n  /// Exponential approach, so temperatures ramp instead of teleporting.\n  double _towards(double current, double target, double rate) =>\n      current + (target - current) * rate;\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------ emission --\n\n  /// Builds the packet a vehicle emits this tick.\n  ///\n  /// Signals report at different cadences, so a packet carries a *subset* \u2014\n  /// which is exactly why freshness is tracked per signal and not per vehicle.\n  TelemetryPacket _emit(_SimulatedVehicle vehicle, DateTime now) {\n    final signals = <String, double>{\n      'speed': vehicle.speed,\n      'ignition': vehicle.ignition ? 1 : 0,\n    };\n    if (_tickCount % 2 == 0) {\n      signals['soc'] = double.parse(vehicle.soc.toStringAsFixed(1));\n      signals['range_km'] = double.parse((vehicle.soc * 3.2).toStringAsFixed(1));\n    }\n    if (_tickCount % 3 == 0) {\n      signals['battery_temp'] =\n          double.parse(vehicle.batteryTemp.toStringAsFixed(1));\n    }\n    if (_tickCount % 4 == 0) {\n      signals['odometer'] = double.parse(vehicle.odometer.toStringAsFixed(2));\n    }\n\n    // Position reports while driving, sparsely while parked. Accuracy is\n    // usually good and occasionally terrible \u2014 the bad fixes are what the\n    // geofence accuracy gate exists to throw away.\n    final reportsFix = vehicle.ignition || _tickCount % 6 == 0;\n    final fix = reportsFix\n        ? GeoFix(\n            lat: vehicle.lat,\n            lon: vehicle.lon,\n            accuracyM: _random.nextDouble() < 0.08\n                ? 60 + _random.nextDouble() * 180\n                : 4 + _random.nextDouble() * 12,\n          )\n        : null;\n\n    return TelemetryPacket(\n      vehicleId: vehicle.id,\n      eventTs: now,\n      signals: signals,\n      location: fix,\n    );\n  }\n\n  // --------------------------------------------------------------- fleet --\n\n  /// Builds one truck. Deterministic from its index, so the same seed always\n  /// produces the same fleet with the same problem children.\n  _SimulatedVehicle _buildVehicle(int index) {\n    const models = ['eT 1000', 'eT 1500', 'eHaul 400'];\n    const letters = 'ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ';\n    final regNo = 'KA01'\n        '${letters[index % letters.length]}${letters[(index ~/ 24) % letters.length]}'\n        '${(1000 + index * 7 % 9000)}';\n\n    return _SimulatedVehicle(\n      id: 'v${index.toString().padLeft(3, '0')}',\n      regNo: regNo,\n      model: models[index % models.length],\n      // Every seventh truck starts near the low-battery threshold and every\n      // eleventh runs hot, so the alert rules have something to fire on\n      // without waiting for a lucky random walk.\n      soc: index % 7 == 0 ? 14 + _random.nextDouble() * 10 : 35 + _random.nextDouble() * 60,\n      drainPerKm: index % 7 == 0 ? 0.55 : 0.22,\n      tempBias: index % 11 == 0 ? 16 : 0,\n      batteryTemp: 30 + _random.nextDouble() * 5,\n      odometer: 12000 + _random.nextDouble() * 90000,\n      lat: 12.90 + _random.nextDouble() * 0.14,\n      lon: 77.52 + _random.nextDouble() * 0.16,\n      heading: _random.nextDouble() * 2 * pi,\n      ignition: _random.nextBool(),\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/// Mutable state for one simulated truck.\nclass _SimulatedVehicle {\n  _SimulatedVehicle({\n    required this.id,\n    required this.regNo,\n    required this.model,\n    required this.soc,\n    required this.drainPerKm,\n    required this.tempBias,\n    required this.batteryTemp,\n    required this.odometer,\n    required this.lat,\n    required this.lon,\n    required this.heading,\n    required this.ignition,\n  });\n\n  final String id;\n  final String regNo;\n  final String model;\n\n  /// How fast this truck eats charge, in % per km.\n  final double drainPerKm;\n\n  /// Degrees added to this truck's steady-state battery temperature.\n  final double tempBias;\n\n  double soc;\n  double batteryTemp;\n  double odometer;\n  double speed = 0;\n  double lat;\n  double lon;\n  double heading;\n  bool ignition;\n\n  /// Ticks left before the link comes back.\n  int darkTicks = 0;\n\n  /// Packets measured while the link was down.\n  final List<TelemetryPacket> buffer = [];\n}\n\n/// A packet the network is sitting on until [releaseTick].\nclass _DelayedPacket {\n  const _DelayedPacket(this.packet, this.releaseTick);\n\n  final TelemetryPacket packet;\n  final int releaseTick;\n}\nDART\ndart format lib/features >/dev/null && dart analyze lib/features 2>&1 | tail -5",

### User — 2026-09-12T09:22:05.851Z
**result**
```
## 1. Layout

```
lib/
  db/          schema.sql · migrations · DuckDbService (isolate, connections)
  ingest/      PacketSource (simulator) · IngestPipeline · Backfill
  derive/      SQL derivation: latest · alerts · transitions · trips
  query/       read-side queries returning plain Dart records
  features/    fleet · vehicle · alerts · geofences · trips  (Riverpod + widgets)
tool/
  bench.dart           cold start / p50 / p95 / memory harness
  export_ai_logs.sh    Claude session jsonl -> ai-logs/*.md
ai-logs/       uncurated AI conversation logs (deliverable 3)
```

No repository interfaces, no DAO layer, no abstract `TelemetryService`. One implementation each; a swap is a constructor argument, not an abstraction. Query functions return records/freezed models straight from SQL.

### Isolates

DuckDB is a single-writer, MVCC embedded engine. One process, so multiple connections against one instance are fine — readers get a snapshot while the writer commits.

- **Writer isolate** — owns ingest, derivation, backfill. Everything that mutates runs here, serialised, in transactions.
- **UI isolate** — read-only connection, queries on demand and on a *debounced* change ping (250 ms). A 3-hour backlog dump must not repaint the fleet list 500 times.

`dart_duckdb` exposes a transferable database handle for exactly this. Ingest batches are bounded (≤ 5k rows / 200 ms per transaction) so a backlog dump never holds a write lock long enough to stall reads.

---

```
### Isolates

DuckDB is a single-writer, MVCC embedded engine. One process, so multiple connections against one instance are fine — readers get a snapshot while the writer commits.

- **Writer isolate** — owns ingest, derivation, backfill. Everything that mutates runs here, serialised, in transactions.
- **UI isolate** — read-only connection, queries on demand and on a *debounced* change ping (250 ms). A 3-hour backlog dump must not repaint the fleet list 500 times.

`dart_duckdb` exposes a transferable database handle for exactly this. Ingest batches are bounded (≤ 5k rows / 200 ms per transaction) so a backlog dump never holds a write lock long enough to stall reads.

---

### Claude — 2026-09-12T09:24:33.242Z
Ingest pipeline is built and running end to end.

```
lib/core/                     Failure · exceptions · UseCase/StreamUseCase · Result<T> · Clock
lib/features/telemetry_ingest/
  domain/        TelemetryPacket · IngestReceipt · IngestSnapshot · FleetVehicle
                 TelemetryRepository (interface)
                 SeedFleet · ObserveTelemetry · IngestPacketBatch · GetIngestSnapshot
  data/          TelemetryPacketModel · TelemetryPacketSource (interface)
                 SimulatedPacketSource + SimulatorConfig
                 TelemetryWriter (long-lived writer isolate)
                 TelemetryLocalDataSource + DuckDb impl · TelemetryRepositoryImpl
  presentation/  IngestController (GetxController) · IngestBinding · IngestPage
```

`domain` imports nothing outward. Concrete classes are named in exactly one place — `IngestBinding`. Every function has a doc comment explaining why, not what.

**Simulator** — seeded, so a run replays exactly. Injects all four failure modes the brief names: retransmits (identical event time, delivered a tick or two later, so dedupe is tested *across* batches not just within one), out-of-order delivery (held back, original event time kept), drops, and basement backlogs (buffered while dark, dumped in one burst). Signals report on different cadences, so packets carry a subset — which is why freshness is per-signal.

**Writer** — spawned once and kept; `Isolate.run` per batch costs more than the write. Batches bulk-append into two TEMP staging tables via DuckDB's row-wise appender (no statement per row, no escaping vehicle ids into SQL), then everything is set-based: `DISTINCT ON` for intra-batch duplicates, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for duplicates already on disk, the conditional upsert for late packets. Two transactions, watermark last, exactly as §3.4 specifies.

**Verified:** 33 tests pass, `flutter analyze` clean, macOS and Android both build. The real macOS app ran for 18s and left 40 vehicles / 4269 signal rows / 627 fixes / 240 latest-value rows / 40 watermarks on disk — read back by querying the app's actual database file, not from the UI.

The test that carries the design: `ingest_pipeline_test.dart` replays the same feed reversed, in ragged batches, with every third packet redelivered — log, latest, fixes and watermarks come back byte-identical to the in-order run.

Two things to flag. `conn.append(table, 'temp.main')` segfaults dart_duckdb (`unique_ptr is NULL`); the schema argument must be `null` for TEMP tables — found by probe, not by guessing. And the ingest monitor auto-starts the feed, since a screen whose job is showing the pipeline work shouldn't need a click.

**AI logs** exported to `ai-logs/` — 2 sessions, 419 turns, tool calls and results included. The exporter needed `--src`/`--match` flags: Claude Code groups transcripts by launch directory, and these sessions were started from a parent folder, so they sat beside unrelated work. `--match byte_beam_project` keeps only this project's conversations; I checked the output for cross-project content and found none.

ARCHITECTURE.md §1 is rewritten — it previously specified Riverpod and argued *against* repository interfaces. Your instruction overrides that, so the doc now documents what the code does; worth knowing the doc changed position, since you'll defend it live. Everything uncommitted.

### Claude — 2026-09-12T20:04:22.413Z
Fleet home is built. Feature A is done.

```
lib/features/fleet/
  domain/        VehicleStatus · AlertSeverity · FleetFilter
                 FleetVehicleSummary · FleetOverview
                 FleetRepository · GetFleetOverview
  data/          FleetLocalDataSource (the SQL) + DuckDb impl
                 FleetVehicleSummaryModel · FleetRepositoryImpl
  presentation/  FleetController · FleetBinding · FleetPage
                 StatusChip/AlertBadge · FleetFilterBar · VehicleTile · FleetEmptyState
lib/core/db/database_pulse.dart
```

Fleet is now home; the ingest monitor moved behind an app-bar action.

**Status and counts are both SQL.** One `scored` CTE — pivot `vehicle_signal_latest` with `FILTER`, union in `location_fix` for the vehicle-level last ping, cross-join thresholds from `signal_spec` — then two queries over it: `GROUP BY status` for the chips, `WHERE status = …` for the rows. Counts span the whole fleet, never just what's on screen; there's a test for that, because counting the returned rows is the easy bug.

**A test forced a design correction.** I had the status ladder checking each signal against its own `signal_spec.max_age_sec` (5 min). But OFFLINE is a 10-minute window, so that leaves a dead band: a truck reporting every six minutes is online yet every signal is stale, and it reads STOPPED while visibly driving. The ladder now scores freshness against the same 10-minute window — status is a vehicle-level claim, so it gets the vehicle's liveness window. The alert badge keeps the per-signal window, since the brief scopes thresholds to fresh readings and a threshold is a claim about one signal. That's logged as ambiguity 14 in ARCHITECTURE.md, and ambiguity 1 now names which window it meant.

**Refresh** goes through `DatabasePulse` — the writer bumps a counter after commit, the fleet controller debounces it at 250 ms. A backlog dump commits several batches back to back and repaints once; there's a test that eight pings produce one reload.

**Verified:** 73 tests pass (20 SQL status/badge/chip cases, 5 controller, 7 widget, 8 end-to-end), `flutter analyze` clean, macOS and Android both build. The end-to-end test runs simulator → writer isolate → DuckDB → fleet query with nothing stubbed; I also ran the real macOS app and pointed the fleet query at the database it left behind: 40 vehicles, 14 moving / 13 idle / 13 stopped / 0 offline summing to 40, 4 badges on the low-battery trucks the simulator plants.

I could not take a screenshot — `screencapture` is blocked by screen-recording permission for this terminal, so the visual check is the widget tests plus that real-data query, not my eyes on the window. Grant permission if you want an actual capture.

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
import 'package:path_provider/path_provider.dart';

import 'core/db/database_pulse.dart';
import 'db/fleet_db.dart';
import 'features/fleet/presentation/bindings/fleet_binding.dart';
import 'features/fleet/presentation/pages/fleet_page.dart';
import 'features/telemetry_ingest/presentation/bindings/ingest_binding.dart';
import 'features/vehicle_detail/presentation/bindings/vehicle_detail_binding.dart';

/// Opens the database and builds the object graph before the first frame.
///
/// Deliberately not lazy. Opening DuckDB and spawning the writer isolate are
/// both async, and a screen that builds before its writer exists would have to
/// carry a "not ready yet" state that never means anything useful.
Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  final db = await FleetDb.open(await databasePath());
  Get.put<FleetDb>(db, permanent: true);
  Get.put(DatabasePulse(), permanent: true);

  await IngestBinding(db: db).dependenciesAsync();
  FleetBinding(db: db).dependencies();
  VehicleDetailBinding(db: db).dependencies();

  runApp(const FleetConsoleApp());
}

/// Where the database lives. Application support, not documents or cache:
/// it is app-private state the OS must not evict.
Future<String> databasePath() async {
  final dir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory();
  await dir.create(recursive: true);
  return p.join(dir.path, 'fleet.duckdb');
}

telemetry_writer_isolate\n                           telemetry_local_data_source (interface + DuckDB impl)\n  data/repositories/       telemetry_repository_impl\n  presentation/            ingest_controller \u00b7 ingest_binding \u00b7 ingest_page\nlib/core/db/database_pulse.dart\n```\n\n## Data flow\n\n```\nSimulatedPacketSource \u2500\u2500batch\u2500\u2500\u25b6 IngestController \u2500\u2500\u25b6 IngestPacketBatch\n  (Timer, UI isolate)                                      \u2502\n                                                           \u25bc\n                                            TelemetryRepositoryImpl\n                                                           \u2502\n                                            DuckDbTelemetryLocalDataSource\n                                                           \u2502\n                                          \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2534\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\n                                          \u25bc                               \u25bc\n                                  TelemetryWriter                   db.read\n                                (writer isolate)                (UI isolate, MVCC)\n                                          \u2502                               \u25b2\n                                          \u25bc                               \u2502\n                                       DuckDB \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500 DatabasePulse.ping \u2518\n```\n\n## The writer\n\nDuckDB permits one writer, so every mutation in the app funnels through one\nlong-lived isolate. It is spawned once at startup and kept \u2014 `Isolate.run` per\nbatch would cost more than the write it performs. Each request carries its own\nreply port, which removes request-id bookkeeping entirely.\n\nReads use the UI isolate's own connection. DuckDB is MVCC, so a read sees a\nconsistent snapshot while the writer commits; the fleet list never blocks on a\nbacklog dump.\n\n## One batch, step by step\n\nThe batch lands in two TEMP staging tables through DuckDB's row-wise appender \u2014\nno statement per row, no parameter binding, no escaping vehicle ids into SQL\ntext. Everything after that is set-based.\n\n**Transaction 1 \u2014 the log and the latest values**\n\n```sql\nINSERT INTO signal_reading\nSELECT vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value, CAST(now() AS TIMESTAMP)\nFROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id, signal, event_ts) * FROM staging_signal\n      ORDER BY vehicle_id, signal, event_ts)\nON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;\n```\n\n`DISTINCT ON` collapses duplicates *within* the batch. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`\nagainst the natural primary key `(vehicle_id, signal, event_ts)` collapses them\nagainst everything already on disk. Re-delivering a packet is a no-op enforced\nby the database, not by application code \u2014 which is why at-least-once delivery\nis all this pipeline ever needs.\n\n```sql\nINSERT INTO vehicle_signal_latest AS l\nSELECT vehicle_id, signal, event_ts, value\nFROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id, signal) * FROM staging_signal\n      ORDER BY vehicle_id, signal, event_ts DESC)\nON CONFLICT (vehicle_id, signal) DO UPDATE\n  SET value = excluded.value, event_ts = excluded.event_ts\n  WHERE excluded.event_ts > l.event_ts;\n```\n\nThat `WHERE` is the entire late-packet story for the read path. A packet that\narrives late but measures an older moment is appended to the log and leaves the\ncurrent value alone.\n\n**Transaction 2 \u2014 the derivation position**\n\nCounts the vehicles whose batch reaches back behind the watermark (the replays\ngeofences and trips will need), then advances the watermark, guarded the same\nway so a late batch cannot drag it backwards.\n\nSplitting the two keeps a long recompute from holding a write lock across the\nwhole batch, and enforces the ordering that matters: **the watermark advances\nlast, so derived state is always behind the log and never ahead of it.** A\ncrash between the two leaves log rows with no derivation \u2014 which is identical\nto the state during normal operation and is repaired by the same \"derive from\nwatermark\" call every batch makes. There is no recovery routine.\n\n## The simulator\n\nA fake fleet on a deliberately bad link. Every random decision comes from one\nseeded generator, so a run replays exactly and a failing test can be repeated.\n\n| Fault | How it is produced | What it tests |\n|---|---|---|\n| Retransmit | The same packet queued for release a tick or two later | Cross-batch dedupe, not just the easy within-batch case |\n| Out of order | Packet held back, original `event_ts` kept | The conditional upsert and the late-vehicle counter |\n| Loss | Packet never emitted | That gaps are tolerated rather than interpolated |\n| Backlog | Vehicle goes dark for N ticks, buffers, then dumps in one burst | Bounded batches, and the UI surviving a burst |\n\nVehicles report signals on different cadences \u2014 speed and ignition every tick,\nSOC every second, battery temperature every third, odometer every fourth \u2014 so a\npacket carries a *subset* of signals. That is not decoration: it is the reason\nfreshness has to be tracked per signal rather than per vehicle. Every seventh\ntruck starts near the low-battery threshold and every eleventh runs hot, so the\nthreshold paths have material without waiting for a lucky random walk.\n\n## Decisions\n\n| Decision | Why | Rejected |\n|---|---|---|\n| Natural-key PK on the log | Makes idempotency a database constraint instead of a code path, so at-least-once delivery suffices | Dedupe in Dart against a recent-packet set \u2014 correct until the set is evicted |\n| Staging tables + appender | One `INSERT \u2026 SELECT` per target instead of a statement per row; no SQL string building around vehicle ids | Multi-row `VALUES` built by string concatenation |\n| Two transactions per batch | Short write locks, and derived state can only lag the log | One transaction \u2014 a long recompute would block readers for its whole duration |\n| Long-lived writer isolate | Spawn cost paid once | `Isolate.run` per batch |\n| Location in its own table | A fix is a triple, not a scalar; pairing lat/lon rows by timestamp is pointless work | `lat` and `lon` as two signals in the log |\n| Start the pipeline from the binding | It must run whether or not its monitor screen is mounted, and `main` can `await` it before `runApp` | `onInit` \u2014 a hook that cannot be awaited, so the first frame could race the roster seed |\n\n## Tests\n\n| Claim | Test |\n|---|---|\n| A redelivered packet applies nothing | `ingest_pipeline_test.dart` |\n| Duplicates inside one batch collapse before the log | same |\n| A late packet lands in the log but never clobbers the latest value | same |\n| A batch behind the watermark is reported late; the watermark never reverses | same |\n| **Any shuffling or repetition of a feed produces identical final state** | same \u2014 the invariant the whole design rests on |\n| The simulator actually injects all four faults, and replays under one seed | `simulated_packet_source_test.dart` |\n| Counters fold receipts correctly; failures surface without killing the feed | `ingest_controller_test.dart` |\n| Building the binding really starts the pipeline and rows reach disk | `ingest_binding_test.dart` |\n\nThat last one exists because every other test passed while a running app\ningested nothing. Unit tests cannot see wiring.\n\n## Known limits\n\n* No backend, so no outbox \u2014 see ARCHITECTURE.md \u00a73.7. The cursor mechanism is\n  real because the simulator is a positioned, replayable source.\n* The watermark advances with no derivation behind it yet. Derived tables are\n  class D \u2014 dropped and rebuilt \u2014 so the first derivation pass rebuilds from\n  the log regardless.\n* `DatabasePulse` is a counter, not a change feed. It says \"something was\n  written\", not what; every reader re-queries. Fine at this scale, and the\n  place to look first if refresh cost ever matters.\nMD\nwc -l docs/01-telemetry-ingest.md",

Vehicle detail is built, and the docs are written.

```
lib/features/vehicle_detail/          domain · data · presentation (13 files)
lib/db/vehicle_status_sql.dart        status ladder, extracted and now shared
docs/                                 README + one document per feature
```

**Readings register** is driven by a LEFT JOIN *from* `signal_spec`, not a hard-coded list — adding a signal to config adds a row, and a signal that has never reported still gets one, which is exactly the "—, no pill" case. Order in the `CASE` is the substance: **staleness is checked before thresholds.** 4% SOC that arrived 40 minutes ago is STALE, not ALERT — asserting "alert" claims something about a value we no longer trust, and "normal" claims the opposite. That's why STALE is a third verdict rather than a flag, and why its pill is grey. Last ping gets an age but no pill; the status chip beside it already makes the liveness claim.

**History** is the one query that touches the event log, bucketed in SQL. Two corrections, both caught by running it rather than reasoning: bucket width has to come from the span the data actually covers (a freshly started app has 20 seconds of history inside a 24-hour window and collapsed to one point), and buckets align to the first reading rather than absolute epoch, or the partial bucket at each end puts the count one over the cap. Sparkline is ~40 lines of `CustomPainter` on a fixed 0–100% axis — auto-scaling makes a battery drifting 61→63% look like a cliff.

**The status ladder moved to `lib/db/`.** The detail header and the fleet list make the same claim about the same vehicle; two copies of that `CASE` would drift.

**Two things worth knowing.** DuckDB 1.2.1 cannot resolve a *second* named parameter in a statement opening with `WITH` — it reports two parameters, then fails the name lookup. Everything is now positional `$1`/`$2`, with the contract documented on the shared CTE. And I moved ingest startup out of `onInit` into the binding: `onInit` can't be awaited, so `main()` reached `runApp` while the roster seed was still in flight. That's a real race regardless; I first blamed it for a run that ingested nothing, but I couldn't reproduce that run afterward, so treat the lifecycle story as unconfirmed — the explicit `await controller.bootstrap()` is the right shape either way. It's now pinned by `ingest_binding_test.dart`, which exists because every other test passed while a running app wrote nothing.

**Verified:** 108 tests, analyzer clean, macOS builds and runs. Queried the register straight from the database the real app left behind — SOC 14.7% → ALERT, everything else NORMAL, 35 log readings into 26 points.

**Docs** — `docs/01`–`03`, same shape each: what it does, files, data flow, the SQL, decisions with rejected alternatives, a table mapping every claim to the test that pins it, and known limits. The index lists the three unbuilt features so the gap is explicit.

skipped: history is SOC-only and the window is a fixed 24h — both are parameters, not redesigns. AI logs refreshed; everything uncommitted.

   const offlineAfter = 'INTERVAL 10 MINUTE';
   -- scoredCte: latest (FILTER pivot) → ping (signals UNION location_fix) → spec → scored
   CASE
     WHEN p.last_ping IS NULL OR p.last_ping < $1 - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE THEN 'OFFLINE'
     WHEN l.speed_ts >= $1 - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE AND l.speed > 0 THEN 'MOVING'
     WHEN l.speed_ts >= $1 - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE AND l.speed = 0
      AND l.ignition_ts >= $1 - INTERVAL 10 MINUTE AND l.ignition = 1 THEN 'IDLE'
     ELSE 'STOPPED'
   END AS status,
   CASE
     WHEN l.battery_temp_ts >= $1 - to_seconds(s.battery_temp_age)
      AND l.battery_temp > s.temp_crit_hi THEN 'critical'
     WHEN l.soc_ts >= $1 - to_seconds(s.soc_age) AND l.soc < s.soc_crit_lo THEN 'critical'
     WHEN l.soc_ts >= $1 - to_seconds(s.soc_age) AND l.soc < s.soc_warn_lo THEN 'warning'
     ELSE NULL
   END AS alert_severity
   ```

## 6. Alerts

Evaluated over `vehicle_signal_latest ⋈ signal_spec`, **fresh readings only**, after every ingest batch.

| Alert | Condition | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `battery_low` | SOC < 20 % | warning |
| `battery_low` | SOC < 10 % | **critical** (same row, escalated) |
| `battery_overheat` | battery_temp > 45 °C | critical |

The two SOC alerts are one row whose `severity` moves warning ⇄ critical. Recovering from 8 % to 15 % de-escalates in place; it does not resolve and re-raise.

**Dismissal.** Sheet order is fixed: *I am on it* · *Wrong alert* · *Something else…*. The dismissal is written to DuckDB immediately and UNDO clears `dismissed_at`. It is not held in memory for 5 seconds — local-first means the database is the truth, and if the app dies mid-window the dismissal stands. That is the honest trade; the alternative loses a user's explicit action to a crash.

**Resolution is independent.** The evaluator clears an alert when its condition clears, dismissed or not. A dismissed alert whose condition never clears simply stays hidden until the condition clears and re-triggers — dismissal suppresses the *episode*, not the *rule*.

---

/// The status ladder, in one place.
///
/// Lives beside the schema rather than inside a feature because it is a
/// property of the data, not of a screen: the fleet list and the vehicle
/// detail header both make the same claim about the same vehicle, and two
/// copies of this `CASE` would eventually disagree.
library;

/// How long without any report before a vehicle counts as offline.
const offlineAfter = 'INTERVAL 10 MINUTE';

/// The shared prefix: every fleet query selects from `scored`.
///
/// **Parameter contract: `$1` is the instant to evaluate freshness against**,
/// and a statement built on this CTE binds it first. Numbered parameters
/// rather than named ones because DuckDB 1.2.1 cannot resolve a *second*
/// named parameter in a statement that opens with `WITH` — it reports two
/// parameters and then fails the name lookup for the one outside the CTE.
/// Numbered binding has no such problem, and a repeated `$1` still counts
/// once.
///
/// Four stages, each earning its place:
///
/// * `latest`  — pivots the long-format latest table into one row per vehicle.
///   `FILTER` keeps it to a single pass, and the per-signal timestamps come
///   along because freshness is judged per signal, not per vehicle.
/// * `ping`    — vehicle-level last ping is the newest event time from *any*
///   signal or position report (§10, ambiguity 2).
/// * `spec`    — alert thresholds and staleness windows read from
///   `signal_spec`, so they are configuration rather than constants buried in
///   this string.
/// * `scored`  — the first-match-wins status and the alert badge.
///
/// Two windows, deliberately different, because they back claims of different
/// scope:
///
/// * The **status ladder** judges freshness against the same 10-minute window
///   that decides OFFLINE. Status is a vehicle-level claim, so its inputs get
///   the vehicle's own liveness window. A speed 40 minutes old cannot claim
///   MOVING, but a truck reporting every six minutes is still MOVING —
///   scoring the ladder against the 5-minute per-signal window instead would
///   leave a dead band between 5 and 10 minutes where every online vehicle
///   reads STOPPED (§10, ambiguity 1).
/// * The **alert badge** judges freshness per signal against
///   `signal_spec.max_age_sec`, because the brief scopes thresholds to fresh
///   readings and a threshold is a claim about one signal, not the vehicle.
///
/// STOPPED is the `ELSE`: both "ignition off" and the documented fallback when
/// the deciding signals are too stale to judge.
const scoredCte =
    '''
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT vehicle_id,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc,
         max(event_ts) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc_ts,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'range_km')     AS range_km,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'speed')        AS speed,
         max(event_ts) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'speed')        AS speed_ts,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'ignition')     AS ignition,
         max(event_ts) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'ignition')     AS ignition_ts,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'battery_temp') AS battery_temp,
         max(event_ts) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'battery_temp') AS battery_temp_ts,

  FROM vehicle_signal_latest
  GROUP BY vehicle_id
),
ping AS (
  SELECT vehicle_id, max(event_ts) AS last_ping
  FROM (
    SELECT vehicle_id, last_signal_ts AS event_ts FROM latest
    UNION ALL
    SELECT vehicle_id, max(event_ts) AS event_ts FROM location_fix GROUP BY vehicle_id
  )
  GROUP BY vehicle_id
),
spec AS (

import 'dart:isolate';

import 'package:dart_duckdb/dart_duckdb.dart';

import 'schema.dart';

/// The embedded database. One instance per process — DuckDB takes a file lock,
/// so extra isolates attach through [transferable] rather than reopening.
///
/// This library is deliberately Flutter-free so the DB tests run on the plain
/// Dart VM. The app supplies the file path (see `lib/main.dart`).
class FleetDb {
  FleetDb._(this._db, this.read);

  final Database _db;

  /// Read-only-by-convention connection for the UI isolate. DuckDB is MVCC,
  /// so this sees a consistent snapshot while the writer commits.
  final Connection read;

  /// Pass to [inIsolate] to get a connection on another isolate.
  TransferableDatabase get transferable => _db.transferable;

  /// Opens [path] (`:memory:` for a throwaway db) and migrates it forward.
  static Future<FleetDb> open(String path) async {
    final db = await duckdb.open(path);
    final conn = await duckdb.connect(db);
    await _migrate(conn);
    return FleetDb._(db, conn);
  }

  /// Runs [job] on its own isolate with its own connection.
  ///
  /// [job] must be a top-level or static function: it is sent across an
  /// isolate boundary, so anything it closes over has to be sendable too.
  static Future<R> inIsolate<R>(
    TransferableDatabase transferable,
    Future<R> Function(Connection) job,
  ) {
    return Isolate.run(() async {
      final conn = await duckdb.connectWithTransferred(transferable);
      try {
        return await job(conn);
      } finally {
        await conn.dispose();
      }
    });
  }

  Future<void> close() async {
    await read.dispose();
    await _db.dispose();
  }
}

/// Forward-only migrations, applied in one transaction each so a crash
/// mid-upgrade leaves the previous version intact rather than a half-schema.
Future<void> _migrate(Connection conn) async {
  await conn.execute(
    'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)',
  );
  final result = await conn.query(
    'SELECT coalesce(max(version), 0) FROM schema_version',
  );
  final applied = (result.fetchOne()!.first as num).toInt();

  for (var version = applied + 1; version <= migrations.length; version++) {
    await conn.execute('BEGIN TRANSACTION');
    try {
      await conn.execute(migrations[version - 1]);
      await conn.execute('INSERT INTO schema_version VALUES ($version)');
      await conn.execute('COMMIT');
    } catch (_) {
      await conn.execute('ROLLBACK');
      rethrow;
    }
  }
}
